$comment: The wake decision, which is where polling loops and lost comments both come from. Six cases: two that must wake, four that must not — and every 'must not' names the reason, because a silent non-wake is indistinguishable from a broken poller.

expected.reason: review comment on an older head still critiques the change
expected.why: Suppressing it loses a human's comment, which is the worse failure. The pass must KNOW the line numbers may not map — hence authoredAgainst beside currentHead, and headMismatch in the receipt.

event.body: add a test for the refusal path

expected.reason: review comment on the current head

cases.name: already-consumed
cases.why: An overlapping poll window returns the same event again. Without this, every wake doubles.

cases.name: self-authored

expected.reason: actor is this workstream's own bot identity

cases.why: The poller sees the foreman's own comment on the next tick. A foreman that wakes on its own output is an infinite loop with extra steps.

cases.name: blocked-on-desk

expected.reason: phase is blocked; the desk answer is the next event

cases.why: Record it and wait. Starting a pass while a human decision is pending is how a blocked workstream quietly resumes and contradicts the answer it was waiting for.

cases.name: cap-stopped
cases.why: A cap stop is a state, not a typo. The event is recorded and would be picked up by a pass after the cap is raised — and the reason names the dimension and the counts, not the word 'blocked'.
